timecoded_text_to_speech.text: You're watching CNN, IPN.
This is Blog Buzz, where you get to know about the latest from the world of blogs
and you get to meet some of the best bloggers from India.
We're kicking off the series with a myth-breaking story,
one about an Indian blogger who's making lakhs of rupees and doing nothing else.
Sangita Sarma has more.
Imagine a job where you can drill a lot of bed
and climb back in just as quickly to start working.
Okay, it's not that kind of job.
Welcome to the world of Amit Agarwal,
one of the few professional bloggers in India.
He may not blog from bed,
but the only muscle he uses is between his ears.
And he's got a job that gives him the kind of freedom most of us dream of.
Agarwal started blogging two years after quitting his job at a software company
and he now owns several lakhs a month.
That's a whole lot of zeros.
So how does Agarwal make his millions from LabNall.Blogspot.com?
It started as a technology blog where you'll now find everything
from ways to get free Windows Vista DVD shipped to you
to creating portraits from your DNA samples.
Not the kind of stuff that makes the newspapers,
but just the kind of stuff that more than a million people want to read every month.
And these visitors also help him make money.
People click on the ads and they go to the advertisers website
and I get some money out of it.
Then there are also ads where they don't have to click,
but as long as they view the page,
they view my blog and the ad appears,
they make an impression, so I get money out of it.
I also get sponsors who like to put advertisements on my blogs.
Working from home decided your own schedule.
It sounds like a perfect profession, doesn't it?
But before you give up your day job to become a professional blogger,
you're a few things you should know.
According to Agarwal, if you want to rewrite your career,
you need to be original.
Post regularly, be consistent with your content and be patient.
Agarwal says his blog only started making money after about a year.
So if you think you can post five to seven times a day
and work 12 hour days,
but you want a little something extra to give you an edge,
you could copy Agarwal and nickname your kid Google.
Our advice not his.
In Agarwal, Suleegha Sarva.

http://www.labnol.org/ 

Amit Agarwal is a personal technology columnist at The Wall Street Journal India and India's first professional blogger. Watch his interview on CNN IBN where he talks about blogging as a career, making money online through Google AdSense and how to become a successful blogger.

Visit Amit's blog at http://www.labnol.org/  or follow him on Twitter at http://twitter.com/labnol
